title: Choose the smallest safe replay boundary
description: Diagnose the incident, select an Oozie retry or rerun operation, and satisfy the evidence gates that keep replay from duplicating external effects or deleting useful output.

actions.label: Resume a manual-retry workflow
actions.detail: Resume the suspended workflow after diagnosing an action start or end error classified for manual retry.

actions.label: Rerun failed workflow nodes
actions.detail: Create a workflow rerun that skips nodes whose prior transition was successful.

actions.label: Rerun coordinator action with refresh
actions.detail: Return the selected terminal action to WAITING and recalculate its data dependencies.

actions.label: Reconcile, then rerun failed nodes
actions.detail: Establish the external commit state before replaying an ambiguous action.

scenarios.label: Late input timed out
scenarios.detail: The coordinator action reached TIMEDOUT before the input marker arrived.
scenarios.symptom: Action 42 is TIMEDOUT, but the producer has now committed the expected partition.
evidence: The coordinator nominal time maps to the intended input URI.
The producer-owned completion marker exists and is newer than the partial files.
The previous action never submitted a workflow job.
scenarios.safeResult: Refresh re-evaluates the dataset dependency for the same nominal slot. Preserving output is safe only because reconciliation proved that no prior workflow committed it.
scenarios.unsafeResult: A workflow-level rerun cannot repair a coordinator action that never materialized the intended workflow.

scenarios.label: Transient action-start failure
scenarios.detail: A ResourceManager outage interrupted launch before business work began.
scenarios.symptom: The action is eligible for manual retry and has no downstream side effect.
evidence: The action error code is classified as retryable in the deployed Oozie policy.
YARN confirms that no application reached RUNNING.
The workflow definition and input parameters are unchanged.
scenarios.safeResult: Retrying the existing action attempt keeps the replay boundary narrow and preserves the workflow graph state.
scenarios.unsafeResult: A broader rerun discards useful state without addressing a simple action-start retry.

scenarios.label: Deterministic workflow defect
scenarios.detail: A malformed query or path fails every attempt until the deployed application changes.
scenarios.symptom: The same action fails with the same deterministic error across attempts.
evidence: The action log identifies a deterministic configuration or code defect.
Previously successful nodes produced versioned, reusable output.
The patched workflow definition validates before deployment.
scenarios.safeResult: The patched workflow reruns failed nodes while retaining successful transitions; idempotent destinations protect any retried external writes.
scenarios.unsafeResult: Retrying unchanged code repeats the deterministic failure, while a full replay needlessly repeats successful work.

scenarios.label: Ambiguous external commit
scenarios.detail: The action lost acknowledgement after the destination may have committed.
scenarios.symptom: Oozie reports failure, but the remote billing write may already exist.
evidence: The action log shows the request ID and the disconnect point.
The destination can be queried by the stable business operation ID.
Output counts and audit records can distinguish committed from missing effects.
scenarios.safeResult: Reconciliation establishes destination truth, and the stable operation ID makes replay converge instead of charging twice.
scenarios.unsafeResult: Blind replay can duplicate an already committed external business operation.

notice: Oozie rerun operations change orchestration state; they do not make remote APIs or file publication exactly once. Capture logs and destination evidence before altering the failed job.
